subject: Sizing ask: committed capacity, tokens/sec headroom and latency fit for Edgeframe pilot
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@edgeframe.ai>

Cc: Edgeframe Ops <ops@edgeframe.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask: committed capacity and headroom for Edgeframe pilot

Karthik —

Following up from last week's demo: our pilot will have a blended workload across search reranking and chat summarization. Quick inbound details:
- Average request size: 350 tokens input, expect 600 tokens output on model baseline.
- Peak burst pattern: short spikes 8–12 minutes, roughly 120 rps request rate during business hours; baseline sustained ~30 rps.
- Expected pilot duration: 3 months; target p95 response SL0: 350ms for chat, 250ms for rerank.

Can you provide a committed-capacity recommendation (slab/GPU count) and tokens/sec headroom guidance so we can size the PO? I attached the token profile CSV. We're flexible on model variant (can go smaller quantized if needed) but prefer to understand the latency tradeoffs and recommended safety buffer for production.

Also, what fallback behavior would you recommend if we hit sustained peaks beyond the committed slab?

Thanks,
Amit
---
Amit Shah
Head of ML Product, Edgeframe
ops@edgeframe.ai

Attachment: edgeframe_poc_token_profile.csv (csv, 18KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Amit Shah <amit@edgeframe.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: committed capacity and headroom for Edgeframe pilot

Amit — thanks for the profile and clear SLO targets. High-level reply first, detailed numbers and an attached slab proposal follow.

Summary (quick):
- Baseline recommendation: reserve 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (1 slab = 2 GPUs in our Dedicated offering), equating to 3 slabs reserved.
- Expected steady-state tokens/sec served (user tokens + generated tokens): ~40k tokens/sec across the reserved pool.
- Peak headroom target: 1.6x buffer (recommended) which gives ~64k tokens/sec headroom before hitting burst policies.
- Latency fit: with that reservation we estimate p95 latencies ~220–300ms depending on model variant for rerank and chat respectively; add ~30–80ms if forced onto a smaller quantized fallback.

Assumptions:
- Model baseline: open-llm-c12-44B (optimized kernels) — we can supply quantized variant c12-44B-q4 for cost-saving fallbacks.
- Typical tokenization: your CSV looked like mean 950 tokens per request (input+output).
- We accounted for continuous batching with 50ms batching window for peak smoothing.

Fallbacks & policies:
- Auto-burst to our non-committed pool (best-effort) subject to extra cost and variable latency.
- Canary rollout: route lower-priority calls to quantized variant when util > 80% for > 2 minutes.
- Graceful degradation: prioritized sampling and response truncation for chat under extreme pressure.

Next steps: Laura and Ben will attach a slab sizing workbook and SLA draft for procurement. Can we book a 30-minute ops call tomorrow to align on procurement dates and an acceptance SLO?

-Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions | Redwood Inference

Amit / Karthik / Ben — attaching the SLA draft and including a compact breakdown here so procurement can see the math without opening the workbook. See attachment SLA-draft-Edgeframe.pdf and the slab workbook Karthik sent.

Key compute mapping (estimates):
- Model: c12-44B (fp16 kernels) — single H100-equivalent GPU throughput: ~12k tokens/sec sustained (conservative).
- Quantized c12-44B-q4: ~18k tokens/sec per H100-equivalent (more efficient for throughput but slightly higher tail latency under certain patterns).

Requested capacity vs recommendation:
- Your steady baseline (30 rps * 950 tokens = ~28.5k tokens/sec).
- Peak instantaneous (120 rps * 950 tokens = ~114k tokens/sec) — note bursts are short.

Reserved plan (recommended):
- Reserve 3 slabs (6 GPUs H100-eq) -> nominal sustained capacity 72k tokens/sec using mixed strategy (mix of quantized & fp16 routing).
- With 1.6x headroom policy that yields ~115k tokens/sec burst absorption when combined with short-term autoscaling/burst credits.
- Suggested token throttling threshold: start deprioritization at 85% sustained utilization per slab for > 90s.

Latency expectations mapped to SLO (p95):
- Rerank (short context): ~180–260ms on reserved pool.
- Chat (longer generation): ~240–320ms on reserved pool.
- If autoscaling relies on non-committed pool: add 60–120ms depending on region hop/backfill.

Procurement notes:
- Committed term: 6 months recommended for pilot; option to convert to annual at a reduced rate.
- SLA itemization is in the attached PDF and includes token-based billing and overage policy.

DocuSign & timing: I'll request the initial PO signature once we lock the slab count and start date. DocuSign link is included in the workbook.

I'll be on the ops call tomorrow at 10:00 PT. Ben, please confirm if the burst-credit model needs any modifications for your billing forecast.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
